ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal AML/CFT requirements are principally governed by the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184, administered by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada. Federal corporate beneficial-ownership requirements are governed principally by the Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, sections 2.1 and 21.303 to 21.307, concerning individuals with significant control. Quebec corporate and beneficial-ownership disclosure requirements are governed principally by the Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1, and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, including beneficial-owner disclosure rules applicable to the Quebec enterprise register. Quebec AML obligations also arise under the Act respecting the Barreau du Quebec, the Notaries Act, and professional conduct rules when regulated professionals perform prescribed activities.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screen the company, directors, officers, authorized signatories, direct and indirect shareholders, UBOs, controllers, counterparties, vessel interests, agents, and payment beneficiaries against United Nations Security Council lists implemented in Canada, Canadian sanctions under the United Nations Act and the Special Economic Measures Act, Canadian Criminal Code terrorist listings, Global Affairs Canada sanctions guidance, FINTRAC risk-based AML/CFT requirements, and applicable OFAC and other foreign sanctions lists where the transaction, currency, bank, vessel, cargo, or counterparty creates relevant nexus. Conduct PEP, domestic PEP, foreign PEP, head-of-international-organization, family-member, and close-associate screening; obtain source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; document adverse-media review; apply enhanced due diligence, senior approval, and enhanced monitoring for high-risk relationships. OFAC screening is not automatically mandatory for a Canadian company without a United States nexus but is commercially and banking-relevant for U.S.-dollar clearing and U.S.-linked transactions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; federal Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre: https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/corporations-canada/en
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Quebec corporation must comply with the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, including French-language requirements applicable to its enterprise name, public-facing business name, registrations, and commercial communications. A name may contain an English or other-language element only within the applicable statutory and administrative rules and must not create a misleading or non-compliant presentation. Quebec filings generally require the enterprise name in the form accepted by the Registraire des entreprises. Federal corporations may use an English, French, or bilingual corporate name, subject to the Canada Business Corporations Act and regulations. Transliteration is not a substitute for required French wording, distinctiveness, legality, or linguistic compliance. A Nuans corporate-name search is generally relevant for federal incorporation and may be required or prudent for provincial name approval.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying a regulated financial, educational, governmental, charitable, or professional status without the required authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Confirm whether the proposed entity will be incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Quebec Business Corporations Act; conduct the applicable registry search, Nuans search where required, trademark search, domain search, and French-language assessment; submit the name request or incorporation filing with supporting consent or authorization for controlled or sensitive terms; preserve the rejection notice, search report, and filing record; correct descriptiveness, linguistic, confusion, legal-form, or regulated-term deficiencies and resubmit. For a Quebec administrative decision, request review or reconsideration through the Registraire des entreprises procedure identified in the decision and, where available, pursue the applicable administrative or judicial review route before the competent Quebec court within the prescribed limitation period. For a federal refusal, communicate with Corporations Canada, submit revised supporting evidence or an alternative name, and pursue judicial review in the Federal Court if an appealable final administrative decision remains legally defective. A rejection does not confer priority over an existing registered or reserved name; do not use the name commercially until acceptance and registration are confirmed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office and service address are mandatory. A commercial virtual office may be acceptable for statutory correspondence if it is a real address in the required jurisdiction, receives and promptly forwards legal notices, and satisfies registry and service requirements. It is not sufficient by itself for a bulk-cargo stevedoring and marine-terminal business. The operating model requires demonstrable port access, terminal or berth agreements, cargo-handling arrangements, equipment and safety controls, competent personnel, insurance, environmental compliance, customs and trade controls, and applicable port, marine, occupational-health, and transport authorizations. A residential address, mailbox-only service, or nominal nominee office presents material compliance and banking risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No published statutory probability exists. For this regulated, port-facing, asset-intensive activity, an annual unannounced physical-inspection risk estimate of approximately 5% to 15% is a compliance-planning benchmark, not an official government statistic. The practical risk may be materially higher following a complaint, licensing application, environmental or occupational incident, customs concern, sanctions alert, port-authority review, tax audit, or inconsistency between the registered office and actual operations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA / Loi sur les sociétés par actions), CQLR c. S-31.1, ss. 9 to 27 (incorporation by articles, contents of articles, issuance of certificate of constitution), ss. 41-45 (by-laws), ss. 89-90 (registered office), ss. 291-300 (registers and inspection); and the Act respecting the legal publicity of sole proprietorships, partnerships and legal persons, CQLR c. P-45, ss. 16-22.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ / Quebec Enterprise Registrar) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of sole proprietorships, partnerships and legal persons (CQLR c. P-45); online portal services.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (statuts constitutifs) filed electronically together with the Declaration of First Directors (declaration des administrateurs) in the REQ 'Constitution d'une personne morale' module.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the QBCA; the board freely fixes the issue price of authorized shares, with consideration paid in cash or property. No escrow account is mandated at incorporation for a stevedoring corporation. However, the applicable Canada Port Authority will require a terminal-operation security (surety bond, irrevocable letter of credit or cash deposit), typically up to 10 per cent of the estimated annual terminal tariff, as a condition precedent to the terminal licence.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION

RESOLVED, that the share subscriptions presented by the incorporators, fixing the consideration for the authorized common shares, are approved; the shares are allotted and issued under the articles; and the register is endorsed accordingly.

RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation is fixed at the address stated in the articles of incorporation, within Quebec, where statutory records shall be kept.

RESOLVED, that [Director] is elected Chair, President and Chief Executive Officer; [Director], Secretary; and [Director], Chief Financial Officer, each authorized to execute banking, registry, licensing and lease documents.

RESOLVED, that the officers shall complete all filings with the Registraire des entreprises, tax authorities and port regulators. PASSED unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Services en ligne, name search module 'Créer une entreprise'
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a preliminary name research in the REQ online registry and, if needed, engage a licensed name-search firm to obtain a non-objection certificate for the proposed bilingual corporate name. Ensure compliance with QBCA ss. 10-13 (distinctiveness, unlawful terms, language rules) and the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11) requiring a French version of the name. Reserve the chosen name in the REQ system against the incorporator's profile for a renewable period of up to 90 days.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name in French and English
Non-objection certificate (certificat de non-objection)
Incorporator's legal name, residential address and identification details
Authorized name-search report if using a third-party provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a name refusal or objection, submit a revised name with the written reasons attached; the reservation may be renewed once without additional fee where the rejection is attributable to registrar error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation and Declaration of First Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - online incorporation filing interface, 'Constitution d'une personne morale'
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and electronically sign the Articles of Incorporation and the Declaration of First Directors, selecting the share structure (e.g., one class of common shares), the share issue price, the mandatory registered office in Quebec, any restrictions on transfers, and the first board of directors. Transmit the full package to the REQ portal with payment of the CAD 339 online filing fee. The corporation comes into existence on the date shown in the certificate of constitution.
required_dossiers: Statuts constitutifs / Articles of Incorporation (QBCA form)
Declaration of first directors with signed consents to act
Name non-objection certificate or reservation reference
Payment receipt for the CAD 339 constitution fee (credit card or REQ deposit account)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ transmits a notice of deficiency (avis de correction), the incorporator must submit amended articles within the stated delay; after two rejections, refile de novo with new signature pages. Fees are partially credited only where the rejection is caused by registrar error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registry Registration, NEQ Assignment and Certificate of Incorporation Delivery
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - register of legal persons under the Act respecting the legal publicity of sole proprietorships, partnerships and legal persons (CQLR c. P-45)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon administrative approval, REQ issues the certificate of constitution, registers the corporation in the Registre des entreprises with its unique Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), and publishes the mandatory legal-publicity entry. Download the official PDF certificate and the NEQ notice from the REQ portal. Verify that the corporate name, share classes, registered office and directors' names are accurately recorded.
required_dossiers: Approved articles bearing the registry date stamp
Receipt of constitution and legal-publicity fees
REQ user account authorization details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate incorrectly records the name, shares or registered office, file articles of amendment under the QBCA and request rectification of the register; no fee is charged where the error is attributable to the registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Quebec Tax and Employer Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online (BRO); Revenu Quebec - 'Mon dossier corporatif' / clicSÉQUR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the NEQ to register for the corporation's federal corporate income tax account, GST/HST account (mandatory once taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 per year), Quebec QST account, and employer payroll accounts (source deductions, Quebec Pension Plan, Employment Insurance, Quebec Parental Insurance Plan, CNESST). File the Revenu Quebec LM-1 business registration form or use the one-stop BRO transfer. Request effective dates aligned with the certificate of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation (certificat de constitution)
NEQ notice from REQ
Directors' personal identification (name, address, social insurance number or ITN)
Estimate of annual taxable revenue and payroll
Corporate bank account confirmation where opened
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax accounts are opened late or with incorrect effective dates, request back-dating of the effective date to the certificate date by written explanation to the CRA and Revenu Quebec; the CRA Voluntary Disclosures Program (VDP) may be used to reduce penalties where disclosure is made before enforcement action.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Corporate Governance and Registered-Office Compliance (First Board Meeting and Minute Book)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Secretary at the registered office in Quebec; compliance monitored by REQ under the legal-publicity regime (CQLR c. P-45)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or adopt written resolutions to: adopt organizational by-laws, issue share certificates for subscribed shares, confirm the registered office address, appoint officers (Chair, President/CEO, Secretary, CFO), and open the corporate bank account. Maintain the statutory registers (shareholders, directors, minutes and accounting records) at the registered office in Quebec. File any subsequent change of directors or registered office with REQ within 30 days.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution (as set out in the incorporation framework)
Organizational by-laws approved by the board
Share certificates with share transfer ledger and subscription agreements
Register of directors and officers
Registered office acceptance letter or landlord consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ flags a late declaration of directors or change of registered office, file the declaration immediately with the late-filing penalty under the legal-publicity Act; where a director fails to act, file a consent withdrawal and appoint a replacement promptly to avoid deemed non-compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Quebec Port Authority (Administration portuaire de Quebec) - Marine Operations and Terminal Concession Department, acting under the Canada Marine Act (S.C. 1998, c. 10) and the Port Authorities Operations Regulations (SOR/2000-55); Transport Canada - Marine Safety and Security for marine safety compliance; CNESST for provincial payroll-side occupational registration
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Marine Terminal Operator and Port Stevedore Authorization (autorisation d'exploitation de terminal et de manutention portuaire) issued under the Port Authorities Operations Regulations (SOR/2000-55), ss. 4-5, together with a terminal operations agreement, tariff schedule and performance security instrument

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Impact Assessment Agency of Canada (for federal designated projects) and Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) - Direction de l'evaluation environnementale for the Quebec authorization track
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category Rating: Registration / Condition-based authorization under section 22 of the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c. Q-2) for stevedoring equipment and terminal operations; escalates to Full EIA / Impact Assessment Report under the Impact Assessment Act (S.C. 2019, c. 28) where new permanent shore infrastructure, dredging, or designated bulk-cargo throughput thresholds trigger federal Schedule screening.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero untreated discharge of wash-downs, ballast water, or bulk cargo residues into port waters; compliance with ambient air PM10/PM2.5 criteria and the Quebec Clean Air Regulation (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 4.1) for fugitive dust; containment and vapor management for volatile bulk cargoes; hazardous waste handling through licensed haulers under the Regulation respecting hazardous materials (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 32); continuous dust and meteorological monitoring at the site boundary where required by Port Authority by-law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the applicable municipal fire safety service (service de securite incendie) under the Fire Safety Act (CQLR c. S-3.4) for terminal offices, crane pads and storage sheds; structural load inspection and certification by an engineer licensed under the Building Act (CQLR c. B-1.1) for piers, wharf aprons, conveyor supports and heavy-lift zones; occupational health and safety clearance for longshoring crews under Part II of the Canada Labour Code (R.S.C., 1985, c. L-2) and the Canada Occupational Health and Safety Regulations (SOR/86-304), administered by ESDC and Transport Canada marine safety inspectors, including stevedore certification, personal protective equipment programs, confined-space permits, and CNESST registration for Quebec-based non-port employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – central federal tax administration (GST/HST, Income Tax) via the Business Registration Online portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html); Revenu Québec (RQ) – Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and provincial tax administration (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/); Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – mandatory Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) registration for any corporation carrying on business in Quebec (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/en/); Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) – export reporting and customs declaration clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entity entering Quebec: (1) assess whether a permanent establishment exists under Canada–home-country treaty and whether 'carrying on business in Canada' triggers registration; (2) incorporate or extra-provincially register via Corporations Canada (federal) or REQ (Quebec), and obtain the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ); (3) register for the federal Business Number (BN) and GST/HST programme account (RT-0001) using CRA form RC1 or CRA's Business Registration Online; registration is compulsory once worldwide taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold, but optional and advisable immediately for a zero-rated exporter; (4) register for QST with Revenu Québec via the enterprise number file (QST account, format NEQ + SRxxxxxxx); the QST threshold is also CAD 30,000; (5) for a port terminal operator, complete CBSA importer/exporter programme account (RM) and bonded facility authorization where applicable; (6) designate a Canadian resident compliance contact for CRA/RQ notices; the corporate tax identifier is the 15-character BN combination (9-digit base + RT programme code + reference) used for all GST/HST filings, plus the separate NEQ and QST identifiers for Quebec-specific filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a resident Canadian corporation (federal or provincial) is subject to federal and Quebec income tax on worldwide income; a non-resident corporation is taxable only on Canadian-source income derived from carrying on business through a permanent establishment in Canada (branch-level tax with remittance of branch profits and Part XIII withholding); no US-style pass-through or check-the-box transparency regime exists; the entity is a GST/HST and QST registrant taxed on taxable supplies at the entity level with full input tax credit (ITC) and QST input tax refund (ITR) entitlement on goods and services used in the stevedoring operation; territorial scope is modified worldwide taxation with foreign tax credits for foreign-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election is available under the Income Tax Act (Canada); relevant statutory elections include: (i) section 216(1) ITA election for a non-resident to compute Canadian-source rental/royalty income on a net basis; (ii) treaty-based domestic law election to treat income as not attributable to a permanent establishment, thereby claiming exemption; (iii) GST/HST joint election for closely related corporations and partnerships (for GST25) to treat supplies between them as nil consideration, with the Quebec QST equivalent (LM-18/VD-58); (iv) simplified registration and quick method accounting elections for small suppliers (ETA s. 179 rules); (v) ITA s. 12(1)(x) and s. 18(1)(u) hybrid mismatch rules aligning with OECD BEPS Action 2 to deny deductions for payments giving rise to non-taxable amounts in hybrid entities; (vi) the Quebec option to centralize GST/HST and QST returns with a single designated reporting calendar for large businesses.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Dual VAT-type system: federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act, complemented by the Quebec Sales Tax (QST, TVQ) administered separately by Revenu Québec under the Tax Administration Act; QST is imposed on the GST-inclusive sale price, producing a combined 14.975% headline burden for taxable commercial supplies in Quebec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — the 'small supplier' threshold computed on worldwide taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated supplies) made in the current calendar quarter and the immediately preceding four calendar quarters (ETA s. 123(1) and Quebec parallel provision); a stevedoring terminal with a permanent establishment, payroll, or fixed place of business in Quebec must register for GST/HST and QST once gross taxable revenue (before zero-rating) exceeds CAD 30,000; non-resident entities without a Canadian establishment may use simplified GST/HST regulatory registration for the sole purpose of collecting tax on imports or claiming input credits of up to CAD 1,000,000 in consideration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time electronic invoicing clearance or digital stamping regime exists in Canada comparable to SdI or ZATCA; however, the following mandates apply: (i) GST/HST returns for reporting periods ending on or after January 1, 2024 must be filed electronically through CRA My Business Account or certified software, with a CAD 100–250 penalty for non-electronic filing; (ii) large registrants (taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1.5 million) must remit GST/HST and QST electronically via EFT; (iii) CBSA requires electronic export reporting through the Canada Border Export Declaration (GCA) and, in the marine mode, the eManifest pre-arrival transmission of cargo and vessel data 24 hours before loading for bulk exports; (iv) the PAN-Canadian e-invoice interoperability standard (Peppol-based) exists and is voluntary for B2B; no fiscal API clearance, QR code stamping, or government real-time invoice validation is imposed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies by the bulk port stevedoring terminal qualify for 0% GST/HST and 0% QST where they fall within: (i) supply of tangible personal property exported in accordance with ETA Sch. VI, Pt. I, with the exporter retaining evidence of export; (ii) supply of services rendered to non-residents where the substantive benefit is consumed wholly outside Canada (ETA Sch. VI, Pt. V, s. 7); (iii) transportation and handling services, including stevedoring, wharfage, and loading/unloading performed in connection with export cargo, provided the service is supplied to a non-resident in respect of goods that will be exported and the service is substantively performed in Canada but directly tied to the export movement; (iv) goods placed in a customs bonded warehouse or transiting through the port terminal under CBSA control; zero-rating entitles the terminal to claim full input tax credits on operating expenses, payroll-related Canadian taxes, wharf improvements, and equipment purchases, and to claim corresponding Quebec ITRs for QST paid on inputs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A or CBSA electronic GCA/eExport data record containing the 12-digit HS code, gross weight, declared value, exporting carrier identifier, and ultimate foreign destination; marine eManifest pre-load reporting to CBSA no later than 24 hours before vessel departure)

Original Negotiable Bill of Lading (or equivalent electronic B/L under the Rotterdam Rules framework) plus mate's receipt and ocean freight invoice evidencing the outbound movement of bulk cargo from the Quebec port (Port of Montréal, Port of Québec, or Sept-Îles)
Commercial invoice in foreign currency stating sale terms, cargo description, and the 0% GST/HST/QST notation referencing ETA Sch. VI
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103, or bank credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the non-resident buyer into the operator's Canadian or foreign bank account

Stevedoring and terminal service contract, draft survey / weight certificate, tally sheets, vessel turnaround report, and Cargo Handling Agreement evidencing the physical loading operation and the foreign-heading of the exporting vessel
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess the exporter within four years of the reporting period, with no limitation where the export claim is misrepresented or fraudulently made; the consequence of failing the substantiation bundle is immediate clawback: full GST/HST and QST are assessed at 14.975%, with daily compound prescribed interest (approximately 4–8% annually) running from the original report date; specific penalties under the Excise Tax Act include: (i) failure to register, a CAD 250 penalty plus 5% of net tax; (ii) failure to file, a penalty of 1% of net tax plus 25% for each additional month, minimum CAD 100; (iii) false or incomplete information, CAD 250 per return; (iv) gross negligence penalty equal to the greater of CAD 100 and 25% of the amount that was sought to be avoided; (v) criminal prosecution for knowing participation in false export claims, with summary conviction fines up to CAD 15,000 and imprisonment up to six months, or on indictment fines up to CAD 75,000 and imprisonment up to five years; Revenu Québec mirrors these sanctions under the Tax Administration Act with an additional 25% gross-negligence surcharge and public disclosure of penalties for registered large enterprises; the stevedoring operator's zero-rating position will be scrutinized against operational documentation, terminal reconciliation reports, vessel manifests, and the 180-day foreign-currency receipt cycle during CRA/RQ export verification audits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada. Canada has no general foreign exchange administration comparable to a currency-control authority. The Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administers AML and anti-terrorist-financing requirements for reporting entities, while the Canada Revenue Agency administers tax reporting, transfer-pricing, withholding, and certain cross-border information obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible for ordinary commercial and financial transactions. Canada generally imposes no exchange controls, capital-import quotas, mandatory conversion of foreign currency, or general restrictions on repatriation of capital, dividends, interest, or sale proceeds. Current-account payments, including trade invoices, freight, port services, and other operating expenses, may ordinarily be settled in foreign currency. Capital-account transactions are also generally permitted, subject to corporate-law authority, lender or shareholder documentation, sanctions, AML/KYC review, tax rules, thin-capitalization and transfer-pricing rules, non-resident withholding tax, beneficial-ownership verification, and reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, the Income Tax Act, the Excise Tax Act, the Investment Canada Act where applicable, and applicable securities or derivatives legislation. Canadian banks may require evidence of source of funds, ultimate beneficial ownership, business purpose, ownership structure, contracts, and tax residency before processing large or unusual transfers. Dividend, interest, royalty, or management-fee remittances to non-residents should be reviewed for Canadian withholding tax, treaty relief, arm's-length pricing, corporate solvency, and required information returns. Quebec entities must also manage provincial tax, language, employment, and port-operational compliance separately from federal banking and tax requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no general statutory requirement to repatriate export proceeds to Canada, surrender foreign-currency export receipts to a bank, convert them into Canadian dollars, or do so within a prescribed statutory period. Export proceeds may generally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be applied directly to permitted commercial obligations, subject to contractual banking terms and tax/accounting records. The corporation should retain export contracts, bills of lading, invoices, customs records, settlement evidence, and foreign-currency ledger records. Export reporting, customs declarations, GST/HST treatment, sanctions screening, and tax reporting remain applicable. There is no mandatory conversion ratio. A bank may nevertheless impose internal documentation, settlement, or transaction-monitoring requirements and may request a commercial invoice, customs reference, export declaration, or explanation of payment purpose.

Operational Account; Foreign-Currency Account; Commercial Deposit Account; Capital Escrow Account where supported by transaction documentation
Operational Account; Foreign-Currency Account; Commercial Account; Capital Escrow Account where supported by corporate and subscription documents

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Desjardins Trust Inc. / Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; Foreign-Currency Account; Commercial Account; Restricted or escrow-style account subject to Desjardins approval

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for supplementary payment and treasury functions; Low as a substitute for a Canadian operating bank where the business requires port-authority payments, payroll, tax remittances, Canadian-dollar settlement, controlled disbursements, borrowing, or local account functionality. An offshore electronic-money institution does not automatically have the legal right to take Canadian deposits, provide deposit-taking services in Canada, operate as a Canadian bank, or conduct regulated payment activities in Canada. The corporation must verify the provider's licensing jurisdiction, safeguarding model, Canadian availability, correspondent-bank arrangements, sanctions controls, chargeback and insolvency protections, foreign-exchange disclosures, data-processing terms, and ability to support Canadian reporting. The Retail Payment Activities Act and related Bank of Canada supervision may apply to payment service providers that perform covered payment functions in Canada, but do not convert an offshore EMI into a Canadian deposit-taking institution. Offshore wallets should not be used to obscure beneficial ownership, bypass sanctions, avoid tax reporting, or route unexplained third-party funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian banks generally permit remote corporate onboarding, particularly where the corporation, directors, authorized signatories, beneficial owners, and parent group have transparent Canadian or treaty-country profiles. Physical attendance is not universally mandated by Canadian law. The bank may require video identification, certified identity documents, notarized or apostilled corporate records, a live interview, specimen signatures, a Canadian business address, a Quebec operating address, or an in-person meeting for elevated-risk files. A Quebec corporation or extra-provincial corporation should expect additional verification of corporate registration, directors, individuals with significant control, signing authorities, business activities, expected transaction volumes, source of funds, port contracts, and licensing. Remote onboarding is discretionary and may be refused if the ownership chain, source of wealth, business purpose, or foreign counterparties cannot be independently verified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership chain, nominee shareholders, bearer-like arrangements, unexplained trusts, or inability to identify every individual with significant control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate and articles of incorporation; current corporate profile or Quebec enterprise registry extract; registers of directors, shareholders, and individuals with significant control; group organization chart; certified passports and address evidence for beneficial owners and authorized signatories; shareholder agreements; trust deeds and trustee certificates where relevant; signed beneficial-ownership declaration; legal opinion or corporate secretary certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital contribution or shareholder loan inconsistent with stated capital, revenue, or project requirements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription agreement or loan agreement; board and shareholder resolutions; capitalization table; funding-flow diagram; audited or management financial statements; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence; originating bank statements; tax residency certificates; repayment and interest terms; transfer-pricing support; beneficial-owner confirmation; expected-use-of-funds schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value or repetitive cross-border payments to unrelated freight, commodity, logistics, port, or intermediary entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master service agreements; purchase orders; invoices; bills of lading; terminal and port-service agreements; customs records; counterparty ownership and sanctions screening; commercial rationale; pricing support; delivery or acceptance records; payment approval matrix; reconciliation between invoices, contracts, and bank statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bulk cargo, commodities, maritime counterparties, or jurisdictions associated with sanctions, evasion, corruption, or trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commodity description and end-use statement; vessel, voyage, flag, owner, charterer, and beneficial-owner information; bills of lading; port-call data; sanctions screening records; export and import permits; end-user certificates; restricted-party screening; anti-bribery certifications; compliance escalation record; documented prohibition on sanctioned persons, vessels, and jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between NAICS or ISIC activity, stated port-terminal operations, licensing status, and observed payment flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan; Quebec and federal corporate registrations; port-authority agreement or terminal concession; stevedoring, occupational-safety, environmental, customs, and other applicable permits; insurance certificates; customer contracts; projected cash-flow model; expected monthly transaction profile; explanation of seasonal and vessel-related payment patterns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of offshore EMIs, virtual-asset platforms, personal accounts, cash-intensive channels, or third-party settlement accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury policy; list of approved financial institutions; account ownership evidence; payment-chain map; provider licenses and safeguarding terms; documented business rationale; transaction-level invoices; prohibition of personal accounts and unapproved third-party settlement; source-and-destination reconciliation; independent compliance review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed persons, public-port officials, government-linked counterparties, or unusual commissions and facilitation payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP and sanctions screening; senior-management approval; beneficial-ownership records; anti-corruption risk assessment; written commission agreement; services evidence; arm's-length pricing; conflict-of-interest declarations; gifts and hospitality register; payment authorization records; investigation and escalation protocol.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent tax residency, foreign tax identification numbers, missing GST/HST or Quebec tax registrations, or unexplained permanent-establishment indicators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRA business number; GST/HST registration where applicable; Revenu Québec registrations where applicable; tax residency certificates; corporate tax returns; provincial registrations; intercompany agreements; permanent-establishment analysis; transfer-pricing documentation; withholding-tax analysis; authorized tax adviser certification.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity through a Canadian corporate account held in the corporation's legal name using a bank-to-bank wire from the subscribing shareholder or an account demonstrably controlled by that shareholder. Use a clear payment reference such as 'equity subscription under [agreement number]' or 'shareholder loan under [agreement number]'; Canada does not prescribe a universal foreign-exchange purpose-code system for ordinary commercial wires. The Canadian bank should receive the executed subscription or loan agreement, board resolutions, capitalization table, beneficial-ownership information, source-of-funds evidence, originating account details, expected amount and currency, and intended use. The corporation should record the receipt as share capital, contributed surplus, or debt in accordance with the legal instrument and Canadian accounting and tax treatment. Do not combine equity, shareholder loans, trade receipts, and customer funds in one unexplained transfer. Screen all parties, banks, jurisdictions, vessels, and intermediaries for sanctions and AML risk. Convert currency only through the bank or an appropriately regulated dealer, retain FX confirmations, and reconcile the incoming wire to the corporate ledger. Review non-resident withholding, thin-capitalization, transfer-pricing, debt-equity, customs, GST/HST, and foreign-reporting implications before deployment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use the Canadian operating account or approved foreign-currency account for supplier, freight, insurance, port, equipment, and other trade payments. A bank may process a SWIFT customer credit transfer traditionally evidenced by MT103 data, although payment messaging is increasingly delivered through ISO 20022 formats such as pacs.008; the bank's current format controls the transaction. Include accurate ordering-customer, beneficiary, intermediary-bank, invoice, contract, and payment-purpose information. For documentary trade, use a commercial letter of credit issued or advised through an acceptable bank under the agreed rules, normally UCP 600, with document requirements matched to bills of lading, commercial invoices, packing lists, certificates of origin, inspection certificates, insurance documents, and port or customs records. For open-account trade, use approved counterparties, dual authorization, three-way matching of contract, invoice, and receipt or service evidence, and sanctions screening before release. CAD domestic payments may use Canadian clearing systems, including Lynx for eligible high-value payments and other bank-supported EFT channels; the bank should determine rail eligibility. Maintain records sufficient for CRA, Revenu Québec, customs, audit, FINTRAC inquiries, and transfer-pricing support. Confirm whether withholding tax, GST/HST, non-resident service rules, or import documentation applies before paying foreign service providers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD and CAD/other-currency forward contracts with a Canadian bank or appropriately regulated dealer, supported by a documented underlying exposure, approved counterparty limits, confirmation, valuation, collateral terms where applicable, and accounting treatment.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or markets where physical delivery is restricted or commercially impractical, subject to counterparty eligibility, applicable Canadian provincial derivatives rules, trade-reporting or documentation requirements, sanctions screening, and a demonstrable hedging purpose. NDF settlement should be based on an agreed benchmark and should not be used to evade foreign-exchange controls in another jurisdiction.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for funding or long-dated exposure, documented under an ISDA Master Agreement with appropriate schedule, credit-support terms, collateral arrangements, valuation methodology, termination provisions, and board-approved risk limits.

Currency options, collars, and option-based hedges where permitted by the counterparty and applicable provincial securities or derivatives law, with explicit approval of premium risk, knock-in or knock-out features, maximum loss, liquidity, and accounting consequences.

Spot foreign-exchange conversions for operational settlement, subject to bank KYC, sanctions screening, transaction records, and segregation of trading authority from payment release authority. The corporation should maintain a written treasury policy prohibiting speculative positions, setting tenor and counterparty limits, requiring exposure documentation, and requiring independent confirmation and periodic mark-to-market review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the enterprise registration anniversary date (immatriculation date).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 78 in addition to the annual fee; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off (radiation), publication of the default, and potential continued dissolution of the corporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal) and provincial corporate return (CO-17)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the fiscal year-end; annual instalments are due separately.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty: 5% of unpaid balance owing plus 1% per full month (maximum 12 months); a repeated failure to file increases the penalty to 10% plus $50 per month; sustained non-filing may lead to prosecution and to the commencement of forced administrative dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Payroll Summaries T4 (federal) and RL-1 (Quebec) for employee compensation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Québec (RQ)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of February following the calendar year for T4; RL-1 reconciliation is due by the same date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late T4 filing penalty is $25 per slip, minimum $100 and maximum $1,000; RL-1 late filing penalties begin at $250 plus per-slip amounts; false or omitted declarations may attract negligence penalties and criminal proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), a private non-distributing business corporation is exempt from the mandatory independent audit if all shareholders unanimously consent. A compulsory audit is required for a distributing (publicly listed) corporation or when shareholders holding at least 10% of the voting rights demand an audit. There is no revenue or asset threshold alone that compulsorily triggers an external audit for a private Quebec corporation, although external audit may be contractually required by lenders or port authorities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP as set out in the CPA Canada Handbook: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for enterprises that are publicly accountable, or the Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for private companies. Annual financial statements must be prepared and presented to shareholders at the annual meeting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual declaration to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec must confirm the updated list of officers, directors, and individuals having ultimate control or beneficial ownership. Any share transfer affecting significant control must be reflected in the annual declaration. This annual filing serves as the single Quebec statutory confirmation for UBO status and shareholding changes; no separate federal UBO annual return is filed for a private business corporation.
